page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 48 MB of L3 cache, and 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The server includes a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-threaded compute throughput alongside expected scaling constraints under multi-core loads. The instance achieved a single-core score of 1,566.0 in Geekbench and 1,876.59 in stress-ng, reflecting median single-core performance. Under full multi-threaded demand, it scored 3,365.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 5,890.72 in the PassMark CPU test. Memory bandwidth reaches 31.76 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 25.49 GB/sec for uncached writes on 256 MB blocks. Application metrics show 3.97 million operations per second for Redis SET workloads and 6.28 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its compute-oriented resource balance and lack of included local disk space, the ecs.c7.xlarge is cost-efficient for tasks requiring dedicated CPU execution without high memory footprints or fast local scratch disks. Persistent data operations require network-attached block storage. The instance profile aligns with front-end web serving, microservices, continuous integration workers, light application backends, and moderate batch processing pipelines.
